summary: A well-built Academic Reading paper: three original passages of 888, 935 and 941 words (pencil history, repair cafes, the cost of interruptions), with difficulty rising from a factual history to an argued psychology text. Keys were sound; the main faults were two pairs of Yes/No/Not Given questions printed out of passage order, plus several broken or weak paraphrase pairs. All of these are now fixed.
strengths: Passage lengths and register match Cambridge Academic texts; passage 3 has C1 argument structure (concession, rebuttal, 'Nor will any single fix...').
Good mix of question types: note completion, T/F/NG, matching information, summary completion, matching people, MCQ, Y/N/NG and sentence endings.
NOT GIVEN items (Q9, Q13, Q33) are genuinely unaddressed rather than contradicted; FALSE items (Q7, Q11) are clearly contradicted.
MCQ distractors reuse the passage's own words (Q27 A/C, Q29 D), which is the real IELTS trap.
Matching people has one unused name (Nkemdirim), as the real test does.

issues.problem: Y/N/NG Q31 and Q32 were out of passage order: Q32's evidence ('running on reduced capacity') comes before Q31's ('Self-assessment in this area is poor').
issues.change: Swapped the two statements (with their keys, explain, evidence, vocab) so Q31 = 'Concentration returns to its full level...' (NO) and Q32 = 'People generally underestimate...' (YES).

issues.problem: Y/N/NG Q34 and Q35 were out of passage order: 'prevents a week of work in the wrong direction' comes before 'Nor will any single fix do the job' in the last paragraph.
issues.change: Swapped them: Q34 = 'Certain interruptions prevent more serious mistakes' (YES), Q35 = 'Switching off notifications is enough on its own...' (NO). Y/N/NG keys now run NO, YES, NG, YES, NO.

issues.problem: Paraphrase pair 'no single fix will do the job' is not in the passage (the text says 'Nor will any single fix do the job').
issues.change: Pair is now ['Nor will any single fix do the job', 'is enough on its own'].

issues.problem: Paraphrase pair text side 'the seconds are trivial' not in the passage.
issues.change: Pair is now ['The seconds spent on the interruption', 'the time the interruption itself occupies'].

issues.problem: Paraphrase pair text side 'engineered to defeat it' not in the passage.
issues.change: Pair is now ['engineered, quite deliberately, to defeat it', 'built to overcome them'].

issues.problem: Paraphrase pair question side 'changes the behaviour of designers' was not in the question.
issues.change: Pair is now ['manufacturers respond by redesigning the products', 'changes the behaviour of both buyers and designers'].

issues.problem: Explain said the sessions produce 'confidence and skill'; the passage says 'competence is handed round rather than bought'.
issues.change: Explain now quotes the passage's wording.

issues.problem: Pair 'oblige makers' / 'manufacturers are obliged' was the same word, not a paraphrase.
Pair 'a higher tempo' / 'completed sooner' did not quite match (tempo is speed of work, not finishing sooner).
issues.change: Pair is now ['They kept the deadline by spending themselves', 'completed sooner but at a cost to the worker'].

issues.problem: Pair 'built again from nothing' / 'rebuilt from nothing' taught little; the real paraphrase is in the verb.
issues.change: Pair is now ['collapses the number of occasions', 'reduces the number of times'].

issues.problem: Option C ('judged less accurate') is partly supported by the later sentence on mistakes in laboratory tasks. D is clearly the better answer because the stem names the studies that compared interrupted with uninterrupted work, but a strong student may hesitate.
issues.change: Suggest changing C to 'C left unfinished more often than uninterrupted tasks' if the owner wants it watertight.

issues.problem: No paraphrase pair: the gap sentence reuses the passage's words ('cut from', 'cedar', 'United States').
issues.change: Left vocab off. Q13 and Q33 (NOT GIVEN items with no matching text) also have no pair.
